facts.text: The agent detects when it is stuck by computing a hash signature of recent (tool, args) pairs, computing an embedding-based similarity of recent tool args, and checking whether recent tool results contain materially new information — at least two of these three signals must agree before the agent is declared stuck.

When the agent is declared stuck, the current turn is terminated and a structured `{:type :stuck-loop :recent-calls [...] :reason "..."}` event is surfaced to the user via `:on-thought` and via a question to the user asking how to proceed.

An empty tool result (e.g. `web-search` returning `[]`) is treated as a low-novelty signal that contributes to the stuck detection, so repeated empty results within a short window are not silently retried.

The `visualize` tool returns a structured map `{:portal-open? bool :data-submitted? bool :data-hash string :hint string}` so the agent can confirm the data was actually received by Portal, and so a missing Portal window produces an actionable hint rather than silent success.

The LLM client emits periodic heartbeats (timestamps) into a shared atom while a request is in flight; the agent loop checks this atom each tick and surfaces `:llm/heartbeat-stalled` to the user if no heartbeat has been received within a configurable threshold (default 60s, env `LATERALUS_LLM_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_S`).

The LlmClient protocol (kschltz.agent.llm.client) gains a `heartbeat` channel — the default implementation wraps the hato HTTP call and writes timestamps to a ref shared with the loop; a mocked client in tests can simulate stalls deterministically.

The agent loop, on detecting `:llm/heartbeat-stalled`, cancels the in-flight LLM request (best-effort, via the client protocol), resets the message queue, and surfaces a `{:type :session-unresponsive :stalled-for-ms N}` event to the user via `:on-error` and `:on-thought` — the CLI does not deadlock.

The stuck-loop detection lives in a new `:guard` slot interceptor `kschltz.agent.interceptors/stuck-loop-detector` that runs in `:enter` after `execute-tools` and has access to the recent turn history via the ctx; it is wired into the default exchange chain in `exchange.clj`.

The `:stuck-loop-detector` interceptor exposes a config knob (env `LATERALUS_STUCK_LOOP_WINDOW`, default 4 calls; env `LATERALUS_STUCK_LOOP_HASH_DIVERSITY`, default 0.5; env `LATERALUS_STUCK_LOOP_NOVELTY_THRESHOLD`, default 0.2) so operators can tune sensitivity without code changes.

The Plugin (kschltz.agent.plugin) schema is extended with an optional `:plugin/slot` `stuck-loop` that plugins can override; the safety plugin is the first example of a plugin that contributes a `:guard` slot, and the new stuck-loop detector becomes a built-in `stuck-loop` slot contributor in the default chain.

Parity tests in `parity_test.clj` cover stuck-loop scenarios: a scripted LLM that calls `web-search` 5 times with nearly identical queries must trigger the detector and produce a `{:type :stuck-loop ...}` event; a scripted LLM that calls `web-search` once and then answers must not trigger the detector.

Integration test for timeout watchdog: a mocked LlmClient that never writes a heartbeat past T=0 must cause the loop to emit `:session-unresponsive` within the configured threshold plus one tick of slack, and the message queue must be reset to `[]` afterwards.

Unit tests for the detection fn `signature-diversity`, `args-similarity`, and `result-novelty?` each have at least 5 assertions covering edge cases (single call, all-distinct, all-identical, mixed with empty results, results identical to prior calls).

A Portal mock (`kschltz.agent.tools.portal/mock-portal`) returns a `{:portal-open? :data-submitted? :data-hash :hint}` map from a `visualize` call without requiring Portal to be on the classpath; existing Portal-dependent tests continue to use the real client.

The existing `llm-turn` retry-on-error text guidance ("Do NOT repeat the exact same call") is replaced by mechanical detection (fact-1) — the text hint is no longer the only defense against tool-call loops.
